q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Short answer — confirmed but nuanced: net sales on 2026-10-12 were much lower than our recent “usual” level, but were actually higher than the previous day.

Key evidence (measured)
- Net sales — 2026-10-12: ₹42,177; reference (usual): ₹104,860 (delta −59.8%). Measured.  
- Net sales — previous day 2026-10-11: ₹34,377 → 2026-10-12: ₹42,177 (+22.7% vs previous day). Measured.  
- Decomposition (measured contributions to the drop vs usual): Gross sales effect −₹66,544 (106% of the change); P&L net sales effect −₹86,988 (139%); P&L return/cancel revenue effect +₹22,304 (36%); P&L ad spend effect −₹27,504 (44%); P&L net profit effect −₹37,816 (60%). Measured.  
- Concentration: channel sub_channel=ig_feed fell from ₹49,246 → ₹4,617 and accounts for ~71% of the change vs usual. Measured.  
- Campaigns/ad names to inspect (measured anomalies): TH-383-SUSPENDER-26SEP-ADV+ and ad TH-383-SUSPENDER-4XL-MAROON_BN520_TM099 dropped to ₹0 from significant usual volumes. Measured.

Why (conclusion)
- The diagnosis found what changed and where, but could not identify a single upstream cause from the available data — “no upstream cause could be identified.” Measured.  
- Correlated signals (hypotheses, not proven causes): sessions, ad_spend and add‑to‑cart events moved with the drop (implicated/correlation). Clicks and impressions were ruled out as causes. Hypothesis.

Suggested next step
- Drill into ig_feed / the flagged campaigns and ad_ids for 2026-10-12 (check delivery status, paused/limit changes, creative approval, or account-level issues) — shall I run that drilldown now?
